chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, raising it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Then he cast a look at the stars, and said: Indeed, I am sick.
He عليه السلام said: He calculated, and so he saw what would befall al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام; thus he said: Indeed, I am sick because of what would befall al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام.

key_terms.إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ: indeed I am sick; an expression of grief and affliction
key_terms.النُّجُومِ: the stars, which he looked toward in order to calculate or perceive
key_terms.بِالْحُسَيْنِ: with al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, referring to what would happen to him
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ: the saying of Allah, introducing the Qur'anic passage
key_terms.مَا يَحُلُّ: what would befall or descend upon

ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Ibrāhīm say, "Indeed, I am sick," according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic words about Prophet Ibrāhīm saying, “Indeed, I am sick,” as referring to his awareness of what would later befall al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. It presents the verse as indicating grief and inner pain upon perceiving the future affliction of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام.
